LIMB_B_BUDGET_CONTRACT_CORRECTION.closes: Section 8.B of the hardening mission - NB-R3's budget/TTL contract.
LIMB_B_BUDGET_CONTRACT_CORRECTION.v101_text_summary: Stated BUDGET_WINDOW_MS (default 60000, admissible_range_ms [30000,300000]) and BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW (default 10, admissible_range [4,30], with a stated lower_bound_invariant) as TWO independently-tunable parameters, each with its OWN admissible range, connected only by an invariant a future implementer was told to enforce via assertion.
LIMB_B_BUDGET_CONTRACT_CORRECTION.what_the_implementation_actually_did: lib/health/provider-touch.ts removes the degree of freedom entirely rather than validating it: `BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW = deriveBudgetMaxProbesPerWindow(BUDGET_WINDOW_MS, TTL_MS)`, where `deriveBudgetMaxProbesPerWindow(windowMs, ttlMs) = Math.ceil(windowMs / ttlMs) + BUDGET_HEADROOM` and `BUDGET_HEADROOM = 2` (a fixed positive margin, not independently tunable). BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW is NOT an independently-settable constant with its own admissible range at all - it is a computed value. At the actual defaults (BUDGET_WINDOW_MS=60000, TTL_MS=15000) this evaluates to ceil(60000/15000)+2 = 6, NOT the 10 v1.0.1 stated as the default - 10 was v1.0.1's own aspirational number, written before the derivation function existed; the code's actual margin (2) is smaller. A module-load assertion (`if (BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW < Math.ceil(BUDGET_WINDOW_MS / TTL_MS)) throw` still exists in the code as a mutation backstop, but for the DERIVED constant it is mathematically unreachable by construction, not a validator of an independently-chosen value the way v1.0.1's text described it.
LIMB_B_BUDGET_CONTRACT_CORRECTION.disposition: SUPERSEDED. PROVIDER_REQUEST_BUDGET_CONTRACT.parameters.BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW's admissible_range and default_value fields are corrected below.

BUDGET_WINDOW_MS.classification: TECHNICAL_DERIVED_PARAMETER. NOT_OWNER_SELECTED. Independently tunable; no admissible range is enforced by an assertion in code, since only BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW (below) is derived FROM it.

BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW.classification: DERIVED. NOT_OWNER_SELECTED. NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_TUNABLE - tuning BUDGET_WINDOW_MS or TTL_MS automatically retunes this value; BUDGET_HEADROOM alone may be changed, remaining a fixed positive margin.
BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW.mutation_backstop: A module-load assertion throws if this value is ever found below its own derivation floor - unreachable for the derivation itself, catches only a future edit that bypasses the derivation.

LIMB_C_HARD_TIMEOUT_SUPERSEDED_BY_HT1_HT.closes: Section 8.C of the hardening mission - the pre-HT-1/HT-2 hard-timeout engineering proposal.
LIMB_C_HARD_TIMEOUT_SUPERSEDED_BY_HT1_HT.v101_text_verbatim: Any exception the touch's OWN probe logic raises that is not itself a classified transport/provider failure - this MUST fail closed to UNREACHABLE (AS-3), not UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is reserved exclusively for the two BUDGET/WAIT-based non-observation producers above; it is never a catch-all for an unclassified internal error.
LIMB_C_HARD_TIMEOUT_SUPERSEDED_BY_HT1_HT.why_superseded: This was Claude's own engineering proposal in v1.0.1, authored BEFORE the owner's HT-1/HT-2 decision existed. The owner has since ratified the OPPOSITE rule for exactly this case: docs/ops/owner-ratifications/M11_TRACK_A_HT_HARD_TIMEOUT_OWNER_DECISION_v1.0.0.json HT-1 states 'If PROBE_HARD_TIMEOUT expires WITHOUT affirmative evidence that the provider/upstream is unreachable or faulty: classification = UNKNOWN' - and the probe's own hard-timeout ceiling firing (an AbortError WE caused via our own AbortController) is precisely a case with NO affirmative evidence, not an unclassified internal error of some OTHER kind. Owner decision has higher precedence than an engineering proposal it postdates and directly contradicts.
LIMB_C_HARD_TIMEOUT_SUPERSEDED_BY_HT1_HT.disposition: SUPERSEDED by the owner's ratified HT-1/HT-2 decision, applied verbatim.

corrected_canonical_producer_set_additio.definition: The shared probe's own PROBE_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS ceiling fires (an AbortError from OUR OWN AbortController, distinguished by `error.name === 'AbortError'`), with no other evidence the provider itself is at fault. Per the owner's ratified HT-1, this is UNKNOWN. A GENUINE transport failure that is NOT our own abort (DNS, connection refused, TLS, or any other rejection whose `error.name !== 'AbortError'`) remains AS-3/UNREACHABLE per HT-2, unchanged from v1.0.1's own correct treatment of that case.

new_technical_parameter_named_but_not_in.why_v101_never_named_it: v1.0.1's UNKNOWN_PRODUCERS.new_technical_parameter named only PROBE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS (the waiter's own patience); the probe's own separate hard ceiling was introduced by NB-R6's closure text in the SAME v1.0.1 document under a different section (module header prose) but never formalised as a named technical parameter the way PROBE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS was.

NOT_OWNER_SELECTED - ratified explicitly as such by HT-3: 'PROBE_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS is TECHNICAL_DERIVED_PARAMETER, NOT_OWNER_SELECTED, and the admissible design must mechanically guarantee PROBE_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS > PROBE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS for every admissible configuration.'

new_technical_parameter_named_but_not_in.mechanical_guarantee: Holds by construction (a positive margin added to PROBE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS can never be <= it), backed by a module-load assertion as a mutation backstop.

LIMB_D_TA19_EXACT_HOST_LIMB_RETIRED.closes: Section 8.D of the hardening mission - TA-19's exact-host limb.
LIMB_D_TA19_EXACT_HOST_LIMB_RETIRED.v101_text_verbatim: The guard is therefore extended by SUFFIX PATTERN (hostname ends with '.supabase.co'), which covers the configured project's Auth host regardless of which ref is deployed, PLUS the exact host parsed from `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` if set and not itself localhost, as a second independent check that does not depend on the domain convention holding forever.
LIMB_D_TA19_EXACT_HOST_LIMB_RETIRED.what_the_implementation_actually_did: vitest.setup.network-guard.ts implements the SUFFIX check only. The env-derived exact-host limb was deliberately NOT implemented: tests/no-real-gemini-network-guard.test.ts's own pre-existing assertion (`expect(source).not.toMatch(/process\.env/)`) requires the guard file to read ZERO environment variables - a property the guard's own header comment states is deliberate, preserved discipline ('There is no ALLOW_REAL_GEMINI_TESTS ... an operator... never unset'). Adding a `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` read to satisfy the env-derived limb would have broken that EXISTING, independently-valuable test property for a limb the suffix check already makes redundant: every possible value of NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL that names a real Supabase project already ends in `.supabase.co` and is therefore ALREADY caught by the suffix check alone.
LIMB_D_TA19_EXACT_HOST_LIMB_RETIRED.disposition: SUPERSEDED. The env-derived exact-host limb is retired as redundant, not implemented as a second independent check.
LIMB_D_TA19_EXACT_HOST_LIMB_RETIRED.machine_testable_substitute: tests/no-real-supabase-auth-network-guard.test.ts asserts BOTH properties directly: that the guard still reads no environment variable (retained from the Gemini guard's own precedent) AND that it still blocks a host with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL deliberately pointed at a DIFFERENT project than the one under test - proving the suffix check alone is sufficient coverage, independent of which specific ref is configured.
LIMB_D_TA19_EXACT_HOST_LIMB_RETIRED.also_closes: The DNS-trailing-dot hardening (M11 hardening mission section 9): the suffix check now strips a trailing root dot before comparison, so `abc.supabase.co.` cannot bypass a guard aimed at `abc.supabase.co`.
